conviction_note: Four correlated findings each point the same way — a doubled tape meeting a print whose sell-side numbers were never marked down to the company's own guidance, a 30-June balance sheet struck at BTC $58.5k, and an inverted net-asset-discount that was the stated reason for the August buyback; because they are correlated (one release deflating one narrative) I size the set at -6.5 rather than the -10.5 sum of the parts, and I hold it well inside the ~11% daily vol envelope because BTC at ~$81k, not the P&L, is now the dominant driver of this stock.

findings.finding: Sell-side numbers for CAN were never marked down to Canaan's own guidance: the terminal Q2 revenue consensus is $53.87-55.41m against the company's 19-May guide of $35-45m, and FY2026 consensus of $269.23m (6 analysts, S&P Global, as of 2026-07-24) requires H2 revenue ~65% above an H1 that will total roughly $98-108m — so both the Q2 headline and any Q3 guide mechanically print as a large 'miss', and investing.com's feed has already auto-published a Q2 revenue 'actual' of $31.20m vs $55.41m consensus (below the low end of guidance) in an article timestamped 2026-09-03 06:27.
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had marked to guidance, the Q2 consensus row would sit inside $35-45m and the FY2026 line would not still read $269.23m with a $1.72 average target and a Strong Buy consensus on a stock at $0.35. Instead the aggregators carry a Q2 number 20-58% above what the company itself told the market on 19 May and an FY number that implicitly assumes an H2 doubling; the wire copy on 8 September will therefore compute a 30-45% revenue shortfall against a stale base regardless of execution, and the +69.8% 20-day run-up shows the tape has been trading BTC beta, not estimate revisions. The auto-published 'earnings missed' article five days ahead of the print is the tell that even the data vendors have a Q2 number in the feed that the equity has not repriced for.
findings.independence: Canaan's own 19-May guidance of $35-45m is a separate document and confirms the gap between guidance and consensus: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-reports-unaudited-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-302776028.html . stockanalysis.com independently shows the FY2026 $269.23m / -$0.77 EPS consensus as of 2026-07-24: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/can/forecast/ . Caveat recorded: investing.com's EPS column for this issuer is unreliable (it shows -0.860 for Q1 2026 against the reported -$0.13 per ADS) and the article mislabels the period as 'third quarter', so I lean on the revenue column (which matched $62.70m, $196.30m, $150.48m and $100.21m for the four prior quarters) and band the finding wide.

findings.finding: The liquidity line is the print's real unknown: cash fell from $80.8m at 2025-12-31 to $43.5m at 2026-03-31 (a $37.3m burn in one quarter) against $106.4m of current liabilities and $21.1m of loans due inside a year, 905 of 1,871 bitcoins were pledged as collateral for $54.5m of secured term loans, and Q2 revenue was guided 30-45% lower than Q1 — so the 30-June balance sheet, struck with BTC at $58,504 on 2026-06-30 (BTC's worst quarter in years, -34% YTD), is where the market first sees how little unencumbered liquidity is left behind the '$130m treasury' headline.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing the cash line, a stock would not double in August on a treasury-value argument that quotes gross digital assets and ignores that 48% of the bitcoin is pledged and that $54.5m of secured loans sit against it. The August coverage that drove the move cited the $130m/$146.1m gross treasury and the March-31 cash figure; nobody has a June-30 cash number, and there is no live option chain and no put skew to show anyone hedging the possibility that it is materially below $43.5m. Canaan also has a $270m at-the-market sales agreement live since 2025-11-04 that requires no per-sale 424 filing, so issuance into the August rally is invisible until this print — and today's -11.0% session (prev close $0.3933, last $0.3501) on no filing and no press release is consistent with supply rather than news.
findings.independence: CryptoSlate independently reached the same liquidity conclusion on 2026-08-06 ($43.5m cash vs $106.4m current liabilities, pledged BTC, ~$28m of buyback capacity remaining, ~$2m executed as of 19 May): https://cryptoslate.com/canaan-can-use-crypto-to-buy-back-nearly-20-of-its-market-value-while-its-core-business-burns-cash/ . The 2026-06-30 BTC print of $58,503.73 is from a third source: https://news.bitcoin.com/bitcoin-falls-below-58000-q2-2026/ . Note this finding and finding 3 both draw the balance-sheet figures from the 19-May Q1 release; the non-overlapping part here is the cash/collateral/ATM channel, not the market-cap comparison.

findings.finding: The stated trigger for the crypto-funded buyback has been extinguished by the rally it helped cause: on 2026-08-04 Canaan justified monetising digital assets by saying it was 'trading below the combined value of its digital assets holdings and its cash and cash equivalents as reported on March 31, 2026' ($130m treasury as of 3 August plus $43.5m cash = $173.5m, against a $144.7m market cap on 6 August), but after a 108.8% August the market cap is $261.0m while the treasury of 1,917 BTC and 3,952 ETH is worth roughly $165m at BTC ~$81.0k and ETH ~$2.4-2.5k — so on the company's own yardstick the stock now trades at roughly a 25% premium rather than a 17% discount, and the repurchase authorisation expires 2026-12-12.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had done this arithmetic it would not be paying a premium to a metric the company published as a discount, and the 20-day run-up would not be +69.8%. Canaan has never disclosed a repurchase figure since the ~$2m executed by 19 May — the 4 August release and the 17 August production 6-K both cite the authorisation and give no amount — so the market is long a 'the company is buying' story with no execution data. The 8 September release is the first venue where that number appears, and because the company's own stated condition for buying (trading below treasury plus cash) stopped holding somewhere in mid-August, a thin or zero repurchase disclosure is the base case and removes the prop under the August move.
findings.independence: Treasury holdings of 1,917 BTC / 3,952 ETH at 31 July come from a different document, the 17 August production 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926097615/tm2623380d1_ex99-1.htm . The $261.0m market cap and $0.3501 last / $0.3933 previous close are from Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CAN/ . ETH at $2,391-2,495 on 2026-09-03: https://fortune.com/article/price-of-ethereum-09-03-2026/ . Shares the 4 August release with nothing else in this file; overlaps finding 2 only on the March-31 cash figure.

findings.finding: The Nasdaq minimum-bid arithmetic is now impossible without a capital-structure action: the ADS must close at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days by 2027-01-11, which from $0.3501 is +186%, so an ADS ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares) has to be noticed to holders around November to be effective in time — and the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since the deadline was granted.
findings.why_not_priced: The deadline itself is in the wire, but the market is treating a stock that doubled as having escaped the problem when $1.00 is still nearly a triple away and only ~90 trading days remain. If it were priced there would be visible demand for downside protection into the ratio-change window; instead the option chain has 6,882 contracts of total open interest and a 0.03 put/call open-interest ratio, i.e. essentially nobody is short this. Canaan has already run the standard pre-reverse-split sequence — it transferred to the Nasdaq Capital Market on 2026-07-06 specifically to qualify for the second 180 days — so the remaining step is the ratio change, and reverse splits in this cohort are reliably sold.
findings.independence: The Nasdaq Capital Market transfer of 2026-07-06, a separate release: https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/canaan-inc-completes-transfer-nasdaq-capital-market-2026-07-06 . The ADS ratio of 1:15 is confirmed independently in the CEO's Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000180299326000005/xslF345X06/form4-06222026_040601.xml

searched_and_found_nothing: Event reality: confirmed, not a phantom. Canaan's IR/StockTitan carries the 2026-09-01 release scheduling Q2 2026 for 2026-09-08 bmo, and Q2 2025 was released 2025-09-05, so a 70-day lag to a Q2 print is this company's normal cadence and there is no timing slip to read into it (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAN/ ; https://www.investing.com/equities/canaan-inc-earnings).

Missing August production 6-K: no signal. The monthly updates land on the 10th-17th of the following month (Feb 10, Mar 10, Apr 15, May 14, Jun 11, Jul 14, Aug 17), so the August update is due ~Sept 10-17, i.e. after the print, and its absence today is on schedule.

Insider buying: real but stale and tiny. CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 500,000 ADSs at $0.33-0.34 on 17-18 June 2026 and CFO Cheng Jin 65,000 ADSs at $0.35 on 15 June 2026 (~$190k combined), filed 18/22 June. EDGAR shows no Form 4 since, including none during the early-August lows near $0.21, so the Yahoo 'CEO and CFO have made significant share purchases' item circulating today is three-month-old news.

Inter-quarter dilution: could not be pinned down cleanly. ADS/ordinary-share count was 690,594,191 at 2026-03-31 and vendors now show ~745-746m, but I could not source the intervening count from a filing — the June POS AMs are exhibit-only housekeeping (No. 6 exists 'solely to correct certain typographical error' in the KPMG consent) and there is no 2026 424B5 at all, because the $270m ATM sales agreement requires no per-sale filing. Flagged inside finding 2 rather than asserted as a number.

Anomaly chased and not resolved into a finding: Canaan files 20-F/6-K as a foreign private issuer, yet five Form 3s were filed in March-April 2026 and three Form 4s in June 2026, and Rule 3a12-3(b) exempts FPI securities from Section 16 entirely. No Form 10-Q was ever filed and the FY2025 annual report came on Form 20-F, so I could not establish a loss of FPI status and dropped it.
Collateral/margin risk on the 905 pledged BTC: live at the 30 June mark (905 x $58.5k = $53m against $54.5m of loans) but defused by BTC at ~$81k today, so I did not size it separately.

Q2 mining-revenue reconciliation from the monthlies: partially built (Q1 produced 257 BTC; June 64 BTC; July 46 BTC, i.e. -28% MoM, with holdings only 1,915 to 1,917 so almost nothing retained) but I could not source April and May production, so no independent revenue estimate.
Any 8-K/6-K, offering, pricing or company release explaining today's -11.0% session: nothing. EDGAR shows no filing after 2026-08-17 and no news item after 2026-09-01.
Reverse split / ADS ratio change or EGM notice already announced: searched, none exists.

Stale-year trap caught and discarded: the gurufocus 'CAN Set to Announce Q2 Results Amidst Mixed Analyst Projections' piece with a $95.36m revenue consensus is dated 2026-08-13 in the snippet but is in fact 2025-08-13 and refers to the 14 August 2025 print. Likewise the itiger 'Japanese contract win, ATM sales pause' story is 2025-10-31, not 2026.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, so the only thing the baseline states is the +69.8% 20-day run-up, and everything I found cuts directly against it: the run-up was bought on gross-treasury and buyback narratives that the 8 September release is positioned to deflate, while the sell-side numbers the wire will print against were never marked down to the company's own May guidance.
